opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. opportunities.title: [Bug bounty follow-up] tarsnap-recrypt can commit old-machine deletes while retaining a stale chunk directory
opportunities.summary: # [Bug bounty follow-up] tarsnap-recrypt can commit old-machine deletes while retaining a stale chunk directory I found a reproducible non-security crash-consistency gap in current `master` commit `0bf0b299fed91139044c81cc6fcdc5521c34d235` (`1.0.41-head`), after the fix for #746 / PR #747. At the end of `tarsnap-recrypt`, the old-machine delete transaction can be committed without any post-delete chunk directory being staged. An interruption or `unlink` failure immediately after that commit leaves a current sequence number but an old local directory which still claims that the deleted chunks exist. Disclosure: this issue was prepared with OpenAI Codex, an LLM, working on behalf of Sebastian Albrecht. The source path, commit state, subsequent deduplication decision, and fix control were independently rerun locally. Sebastian is available to discuss the report and answer technical questions. ## Cause The success tail in `recrypt/recrypt.c` performs: ```c storage_delete_end(SD); multitape_commit(ocachedir, omachinenum, oseqnum, 1, &storage_modified); unlink(odirpath); ``` Unlike a normal chunk deletion, this path never calls `chunks_delete_end` or `chunks_directory_write(..., ".tmp")`

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
